name: Hassan-Rosen Bimetric with Auxiliary Kinetic Isolation (HRAKI)
claimed_mechanism: This architecture introduces a second dynamical metric f_munu coupled via Hassan-Rosen bigon terms to the physical metric g_munu. The MOND dynamics are encoded in an auxiliary scalar chi that enforces the standard Legendre constraint on g_munu, generating the correct MOND force law without propagating scalar DOFs. A second auxiliary scalar s mediates a screened preferred-frame interaction, coupling to the bimetric acceleration a_mu with a coefficient proportional to e^-y. This s-field is purely algebraic (kinetic: none), so it generates the necessary off-ray lensing slip required by the DC-013 theorem without introducing a propagating mode whose kinetic normalization could vanish in the screened limit (P7).
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the Hassan-Rosen sector yields a massive spin-2 mode with a finite, independent kinetic normalization M^2_HR that is constant and does not depend on y. The MOND sector provides the enhanced Newtonian potential. The screened s-field, being algebraic, contributes a static off-diagonal slip to the metric potentials (Phi != Psi) proportional to e^-y * a_mu. Because s is non-propagating, its contribution is purely contact-like in the PPN sense, generating the required lensing enhancement without the strong-coupling divergence seen in propagating khronon or stiff-vector models. The exponential screening e^-y ensures that this slip vanishes rapidly in the Solar System (y >> 1), satisfying the P2 requirement for preferred-frame couplings.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is structurally distinct from all dead classes. It is not DC-001/DC-012/DC-013 (frame-free local/nonlocal) because it explicitly contains a preferred-frame coupling (s, a_mu) that is screened. It is not DC-002/DC-014 (stiff/propagating vector) because the preferred-frame carrier is an auxiliary scalar (s), not a vector, and it has no kinetic term (kinetic: none), avoiding the P7 strong-coupling mechanism that kills stiff vectors (K->inf) and propagating vectors (K->e^-y). It is not DC-010 (khronometric) because it does not use a khronon field; the preferred-frame effect is mediated by an algebraic scalar in a bimetric setup. The key architectural difference is the use of a second metric (f_munu) to provide the massive graviton kinetic term, which is independent of the MOND screening factor, thereby satisfying the A3 principle that PPN-visible couplings must not control propagating mode kinetic normalizations.
